findings.title: AC3's "registers every allocation idempotently" is asserted, never driven
findings.evidence: Ticket AC3: "The derived journal carries one credit leg per advance account and the post-approve registration trigger registers every allocation idempotently." The first half is driven (p931.two: two clara.staff_advance_applications rows keyed to one credit leg; p931.accounts: two legs, one allocation each). The second half is not: nothing in packages/db/tests/staff-expense-claim-allocations.test.mjs re-enters clara._tf_adv_claim_application_birth for a multi-allocation claim. The report's AC3 row cites the #638 replay cells as the idempotence evidence, but packages/db/tests/staff-expense-claim.test.mjs:1048 p638.replay drives clara.admit_staff_expense_claim_work twice under one intent key; it never re-fires the post-approve trigger. The property is structurally held by uq_staff_advance_applications_line_advance plus the exists probe and the on conflict (application_line_id, advance_id) do nothing at 0301 section E, so the accounting risk is low. What is wrong is the evidence claim, against the wave-3 rule that a door's behaviour is asserted only after it was driven.
findings.required_fix: Either add one cell that re-enters the birth path for a two-allocation claim and asserts exactly two clara.staff_advance_applications rows with outstanding unchanged, or correct the AC3 row of docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/reports/wave4-lane02-ticket931.md to say the idempotence of the LIST case rests on the unique index and the on-conflict clause and was not driven, moving it into "Anything unverified".

findings.title: "every advance named must belong to this claimant" gained a second arm the ticket does not describe
findings.evidence: Ticket: "every advance named must belong to this claimant on an enrolled account". Migration 0301 section C implements two arms: (a) the advance's enrolment_id IS the claim's claimant enrolment; or (b) the advance's enrolment is another LIVE enrolment of this client whose btrim(person_label) is byte-identical to the claimant's. Arm (b) admits an advance sitting on a DIFFERENT enrolment row on a string comparison of an attested label. The ticket neither asks for it nor rules it out, and it is the only thing that makes the ticket's own listed default ("advances on different enrolled accounts may be discharged together") reachable; p931.accounts and p931.claimant both turn on it. The implementer named it as a decision and asked for review. It is NOT a loosening: 0221 checked only which ACCOUNT the advance sat on, so nothing 0221 refused is now admitted.
findings.required_fix: Put the two-arm reading in front of the owner before release (arm (a) only, versus arm (a)+(b)), as the ticket report asks, and record the ruling on #931 so the staff-master successor ticket can cite it. The narrow version is a two-line change and one cell, and it makes cross-account splits unreachable.

findings.title: AC5 is not implemented: correctly routed to a successor contract, and it carries real debt
findings.evidence: AC5, as corrected by the owner's 2026-09-19 comment to chatTurn_v22: "The chat tool contract widens to an allocation list in the next chatTurn successor; the tool proposes a split when unstated and parks a question for confirmation; a World e2e leg covers it." Nothing in packages/runtime/workflows or packages/runtime/lib changed and freeze-lint is OK at 312 files. Wave-4 lane rule (b) routes exactly this to the chatTurn_v22 / claraWork_v6 cut at the end of wave 4, and the report's successor contract carries all six required elements: tool name, zod input, door call with argument order, refusal mapping, part kind, prompt stanza. So this is compliant, not a defect. The debt: proposeAllocationsByDate has no runtime implementation or cell, advance_split_unconfirmed has no cell, the World e2e leg is unwritten, and the stableOpKey widening is untested.
findings.required_fix: Carry sections 1 to 10 of wave4-lane02-ticket931.md into the chatTurn_v22 ceremony's checklist verbatim, and file the World e2e leg as its own item so AC5 is not closed by the cut alone.

findings.title: AC6's "from-scratch apply" is proved by a rolled-back prestate probe, not by an apply
findings.evidence: AC6 lists "from-scratch apply" among the required cells. 0301 was first-applied on clara_l02 and then redone four times with CLARA_MIGRATION_REDO; because the prestate is bimodal on its own marker, a redo can only take the "already live" branch. The first-apply branch was proved inside one rolled-back transaction that restored 0221's pre-images and ran 0301's prestate verbatim (report: FIRST-APPLY PRESTATE PROOF: PASS). That is what the wave-3 addendum asks a lane to do, and the same addendum says the integrator runs the true from-scratch chain, so the AC is not closable inside the lane.
findings.required_fix: Integrator: run the true 0001 to 0301 chain on a disposable cluster before the PR and record the result against #931 AC6. Watch section G's backfill in particular: tails T.3, T.3b and T.3c refuse rather than backfill anything they cannot state exactly, and hosted holds advance-application claims this rig does not.

findings.title: Two new head-consistency refusals and the changed-split conflict go beyond the ticket's refusal list
findings.evidence: AC2 enumerates the validator's refusals: exact-sum, claimant ownership, per-allocation temporal cap, typed shortfall naming the advance, and the existing no-advance and wrong-client reasons unmoved. 0301 section C additionally raises constraint allocation_head at claim.advance_id and at claim.advance_account_code when a stated head disagrees with the list's first line, and the recut canonical form makes a changed split an intent_payload_conflict (celled as p931.split.conflict). Neither is asked for. Both head refusals are unreachable from apps/web (toClaimWire always sets advanceId to rows[0]) and from the route (toDbClaim derives the head when absent), so they only bite a hand-built door call; the conflict semantics follow necessarily from putting advance_allocations in the canonical form, which AC1 requires.
findings.required_fix: None required. If the integrator wants the refusal surface minimal, the two allocation_head raises are the removable pair; the conflict semantics are not.

findings.title: The chooser is scoped to claimantAccountCode while the settlement leg is a separate picker, and rows carry no account_code
findings.evidence: #930 AC1: "listing only advances with a positive outstanding balance for the chosen claimant". apps/web/components/accounting/staff-expense-claim-form.tsx:262 filters candidates by draft.claimantAccountCode, while the claim's credit leg comes from the independent advanceAccountCode picker at line 669 with no default from the claimant. Two consequences, neither an AC breach: a preparer who picks a different advanceAccountCode is offered advances the door then refuses with constraint not_this_client (0221's own reason, unmoved); and the form's allocation rows carry no account_code, so every line defaults to advance_account_code and the form cannot express the cross-account split that #931's own default list allows and p931.accounts proves at the door. AC4 does not ask for it, and the lane report names it as follow-up 2.
findings.required_fix: None for this wave. Worth a follow-up ticket: either default advanceAccountCode from claimantAccountCode, or widen the chooser to every enrolled account of the claimant and carry account_code on each row.

findings.title: "the register then shows one discharge per named advance" is satisfied at the data level only
findings.evidence: Ticket "What to build": "the register then shows one discharge per named advance". No web register surface changed in the diff. It holds because the birth trigger mints one clara.staff_advance_applications row per allocation (p931.two asserts two rows, p931.accounts asserts one per account) and the register reads those rows generically through clara.staff_advance_statement and clara.staff_advance_summary, both unchanged. No unit cell or browser walk drives the staff-advances register showing two discharges arising from ONE claim.
findings.required_fix: None required. If the integrator wants it driven, the cheapest cell is an assertion on staff_advance_statement's movements for the p931.two client.

One accounting-relevant reading the ticket never settled, arm (b) of "belongs to this claimant" (a byte-equal person_label across two enrolments), was decided by the implementer, flagged by them, and needs the owner's ruling before release (SPEC-931-B). One piece of residue to delete: the orphaned advanceIdPlaceholder message key (SPEC-930-C). Nothing in the diff contradicts a ticket line, no wall was loosened, and no requirement is implemented wrongly.
